newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica shares calmer, still attractive.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica shares calmer, still attractive.

text.p: Shares in Spanish telecoms operator Telefonica traded quietly on Tuesday after several rocky days and dealers said the stock was still a good buy.

"In the long term, Telfonica is undervalued for us and we recommend keeping it in the portfolio, although short term it could have some ups and downs in terms of the general comportment of the market," one analyst said.

Sector experts said the shares could start gaining again with the announcement, expected imminently, of the operator's choice of an American partner and any delay in the auction for Retevision, Spain's second provider of basic telephone services.

"At the moment, Telefonica shares are behaving more or less in line with the market, ahead of a clearer picture of its international strategy and its competition in the domestic market," another analyst said.

Telefonica de Espana chairman Juan Villalonga said in March that the company was negotiating with nearly all of the major U.S. operators in a quest for an alliance to launch Hispanic operations in the United States.
He said Telefonica would announce the name of its new U.S. partner within a few weeks. Traders see either AT&T or MCI as the most likely candidate.

On the domestic front, analysts say the privatisation of Retevision was proceeding according to calendar -- the company plans to offer basic telephone service by the end of the year -- but there was a certain amount of confusion about the groups aligning to bid for the state broadcaster.
A third factor weighing on Telefonica's share price has to do with interconnection rates for future telecoms operators in Spain and a tariff restructuring that took place two weeks ago.

The restructuring should allow Telefonica to considerably boost its local rates throughout 1998 and, according to analysts, compensate in large part for the somewhat lower than forecast rate of interconnection to its network.

"In the last 10 days, analysts have done the calculations and it seems that the effect of the new tariff scheme and the interconnection prices is neutral," the expert with the international brokerage said.
Telefonica was trading up five pesetas at 3,395 at 1130 GMT on Tuesday.
